Hidden, not disabled — a permanently greyed control in a mode the user deliberately chose reads as breakage. Everything else stays: Restart, Detach (re-parents the chat instead of the console), View Changes, Session History, Show Usage, Set Working Directory and Send Build Errors all run through paths native mode shares
128-- The toolbar is mirrored into the chat tab's composer in native mode (issue #151/v170.0). `RefreshToolbarLayout` ends by building a promoted-button list from `GetEffectiveToolbarOrder()` filtered to `_settings.VisibleToolbarButtons`, skipping `ToolbarButton.DetachTerminal` (the panel's own ⧉, meaningless from inside the tab it opens) and `ToolbarButton.RestartAgent` (the composer already has ↻ `ComposerClearButton`, which starts a fresh agent session — a second restart button next to it would just be a confusing duplicate), and calls `ChatTranscript.SetPromotedButtons(...)` — reading each entry's `Content`/`ToolTip` straight off the real panel `Button` via `GetToolbarButtonControl` rather than keeping a second copy of the glyph/tooltip strings, so the mirror can't drift out of sync. 129-- `DetachToolbarButton` (⧉) is forced visible whenever `IsNativeModeActive`, regardless of whether it's promoted (issue #151/v170.0) — with the prompt box auto-hidden and most of the toolbar mirrored into the tab, it is the only way back to the chat once it has left for its own tab, so it can't depend on the user's toolbar customization. `DetachTerminalMenuItem`'s ☰ copy is collapsed at the same time, since a button that can never be hidden makes the menu entry dead weight.
130-- The composer's own ⚙/☰/⚡ buttons mirror the panel's `ContextMenu` instances rather than duplicating them (`UI/ChatTranscriptView.xaml`'s `ComposerSettingsButton`/`ComposerToolsButton`/`ComposerCustomCommandsButton`, next to the selector row). `ChatConfigMenu` (`ChatTranscriptView.xaml.cs`) and `ConfigMenuClicked` mirror the existing `ChatSelector`/`SelectorClicked` pattern; `OnComposerConfigMenuClicked` (NativeChat.cs) maps the enum to the panel's real `ProviderContextMenu`/`ToolsContextMenu`/`CustomCommandsContextMenu` and opens it re-anchored to the composer button via the shared `OpenMenuAt` helper (`Placement.Top`, since the composer sits at the bottom of the tab — the panel's own dropdowns open `Placement.Bottom`). No menu content is ever built twice; `GetConfigMenuAnchor`/`GetPromotedButtonAnchor` return null (so the click is silently ignored) whenever the composer itself is collapsed (`ComposerMode.Hidden`).
131-- v170.0 shipped both surfaces showing everything at once — the panel's own promoted buttons/⚙/☰/⚡ stayed visible alongside their new composer mirrors, and a manual F5 pass against the shipped build immediately reproduced exactly the clutter the plan's own "Deliberately not doing" footnote had flagged as a likely follow-up. Fixed the same day (still v170.0, since the bump had not been committed yet): `RefreshToolbarLayout` now checks a new `IsChatDetachedToOwnTab` property (`IsNativeModeActive && _chatIsInTab`, NativeChat.cs) and, only when true, collapses every panel promoted button/menu item (all of `DefaultToolbarButtonOrder` except `DetachTerminal`) plus `ModelDropdownButton`/`ToolsDropdownButton`/`CustomCommandsButton`/`MenuDropdownButton` — leaving ⧉ as the panel's sole visible control once the chat has actually left for its own tab. Gated on `_chatIsInTab` specifically, not just native mode, so `ComposerMode.ActionsOnly` (chat still docked) leaves the panel's own toolbar untouched — that's the only surface open in that state. The composer side of the same duplication (its ⚙/☰/⚡/promoted mirrors were visible in `ActionsOnly` too, redundant with the panel toolbar sitting in the same window) is fixed symmetrically: `SetComposerMode` moved `ComposerSettingsButton`/`ComposerCustomCommandsButton`/`ComposerPromotedButtons` into the `fullOnly` visibility group, so they only render once the chat is actually detached. The four selector buttons (`ComposerProviderButton`/`Model`/`Effort`/`PermissionButton`) are deliberately excluded from that group — they're the actual issue #151 fix and must stay reachable in `ActionsOnly` too.
132-- ☰'s composer mirror additionally tracks whether the dropdown it opens would be empty: `RefreshToolbarLayout` already computes `anyInDropdown` for the panel's own `ToolsDropdownButton`; it now also calls `ChatTranscript.SetToolsMenuHasItems(anyInDropdown)`, which combines that with the `Full`-only gate in `ChatTranscriptView`'s private `UpdateToolsButtonVisibility()` (`_composerMode == ComposerMode.Full && _toolsMenuHasItems`) — so `ComposerToolsButton` never opens onto nothing.
133-- `ComposerSendButton` (➤ Send) was removed outright — the composer's Enter key already sends (`ComposerInput_PreviewKeyDown`, gated by the existing `SendWithEnter`/`SendWithCtrlEnter` settings) independent of any button, so the button was pure clutter next to an increasingly busy action row. The placeholder text now says "Enter to send" in its place. Issue #186 (v227.0): `ComposerSendButton` (▶) is back, but only in "Button only" mode (`SendWithEnter` and `SendWithCtrlEnter` both off) and the composer is in Full mode; it sits inside the input box and raises the same `SendRequested` as the Enter key. Settings Apply and a Backup import call `ApplyChatSendKeySettings()` so the open chat composers pick the new send key up immediately (they only copied it during a full composer refresh before). In terminal mode and the docked chat the panel's `SendPromptButton` now sits in the same bottom-right corner of the prompt box (inside `PromptGroupBox`) instead of the toolbar strip.
134-- The above collapse logic lived entirely inside `RefreshToolbarLayout`, but nothing actually called that method at the two moments the collapse needs to happen — `ShowNativeChatTabAsync` and `ReturnNativeChatToPanel` (NativeChat.cs) set `_chatIsInTab` and moved on, so the panel kept its full toolbar until some unrelated event (a provider switch, a settings save) happened to trigger a refresh. A second F5 pass caught this — the panel's own buttons were still there right after detaching, next to the same buttons now also mirrored in the tab. Fixed by calling `RefreshToolbarLayout()` at the end of both methods. `IsChatDetachedToOwnTab` also replaced the two other places that unconditionally reset `SendPromptButton.Visibility` from the `SendWithEnter` setting (`ApplyLayout` in Settings.cs, and the Settings dialog's Apply in SettingsDialog.cs) — both now skip that assignment while the chat is detached, so changing that setting (or just re-opening Settings) can't bring the Send button back next to a prompt box that isn't even shown.
135-- The composer's action row (session actions, selectors, mirrored config buttons) sits above the prompt text box, not below it (moved the same day as the collapse fix, after the same screenshot showed it crammed at the very bottom of the window, underneath the box it controls). `ComposerBar`'s inner `Grid` keeps its four `Auto` rows but reassigns them: `ComposerResizeGrip` stays row 0 (dragging the composer's top edge doesn't care what's below it), the action `DockPanel` moved from row 3 to row 1, `ComposerAttachments` moved from row 1 to row 2, and `ComposerInputBorder` moved from row 2 to row 3 — so, top to bottom, it now reads resize grip → toolbar → attachment chips → text box. Reassigning `Grid.Row` was enough; WPF doesn't require row-ordered document order, so no controls needed to physically move in the XAML. The config/selector popups still open `Placement.Top` off their button (`OpenMenuAt`) — that was never about the button's row inside the composer, it's about the composer as a whole sitting at the bottom of the tab with the whole transcript's worth of room above it, which didn't change.
136-- Round 3 of the same F5 pass (still v170.0): the composer's own 📎 `ComposerAttachButton`/`AttachRequested` was removed outright — Ctrl+V paste and drag-and-drop already attach a file or image, so the button added nothing that wasn't already reachable, and it made even less sense once the panel's own `AttachDropdownButton` (with its "Insert Active File Path" entry) was already gone from view whenever the chat is detached (see the `IsChatDetachedToOwnTab` collapse above). Its removal took `OnComposerAttachRequested` (NativeChat.cs) and both of its event subscriptions with it; `OnComposerFilesDropped`/`OnComposerPasteRequested` are untouched. Separately, the action row's `DockPanel` is now wrapped in a `ScrollViewer` (`ComposerActionsScroller`, `HorizontalScrollBarVisibility="Auto"`) — a customized toolbar plus every selector and mirrored config button can be wider than the tab, and the row used to clip silently past the window edge with no way to reach what didn't fit. `ComposerActionsScroller_PreviewMouseWheel` remaps the mouse wheel (vertical by default, and there is nothing vertical in this row for it to act on) to `ScrollToHorizontalOffset`, only when `ScrollableWidth > 0` so the event still bubbles normally everywhere else.
137-- Round 4 of the same F5 pass (still v170.0), from a follow-up screenshot: two more complaints. First, "the button for attach/detach should never show for native mode" — a direct reversal of Change D above, which had forced ⧉ `DetachToolbarButton` always visible in native mode specifically so there was a way back to the chat tab. `RefreshToolbarLayout()` now gates it the opposite way: `Apply(ToolbarButton.DetachTerminal, !IsNativeModeActive, DetachToolbarButton, DetachTerminalMenuItem)` hides it unconditionally whenever native mode is active, whether the chat is docked or already in its own tab (the old `if (id == ToolbarButton.DetachTerminal) continue;` carve-out in the `IsChatDetachedToOwnTab` collapse loop is gone too — redundant once ⧉ is already hidden earlier in the method). This was judged an acceptable tradeoff rather than something to push back on: a lone floating ⧉ in an otherwise-mostly-collapsed panel read as confusing clutter, not a useful control; the chat tab already reopens on its own via `ShowNativeChatTabAsync` at the end of every native session (re)start; and closing the tab manually still doesn't lose the conversation — `ReturnNativeChatToPanel` re-embeds the live `ChatTranscript` back into the panel. The one real consequence: after closing the chat tab, there is no button to pop it back into its own tab again until the next native-mode restart (it stays fully usable, just docked in the narrower panel meanwhile). Second complaint: "small arrow for scrolling only the buttons, not full ugly scroll bar" — the Round 3 `ScrollViewer` with `HorizontalScrollBarVisibility="Auto"` is now `"Hidden"`, wrapped in a new 3-column `Grid` named `ComposerActionRow` (`Auto` / `*` / `Auto`) with `ComposerActionsScrollLeftButton` (◀) and `ComposerActionsScrollRightButton` (▶) flanking `ComposerActionsScroller` in the outer columns, styled off the same `ComposerSelectorStyle` as the selectors themselves (just smaller: `FontSize="9"`, `Padding="4,2,4,2"`). Each arrow starts `Collapsed` and is toggled by a new `ComposerActionsScroller_ScrollChanged` handler reading `ScrollableWidth`/`HorizontalOffset`, so an arrow only appears when there's actually more content to reach in that direction — no permanently-visible dead-end arrows, and no native scrollbar track competing for space in a row this thin. The Round 3 mouse-wheel remap (`ComposerActionsScroller_PreviewMouseWheel`) is untouched; clicking an arrow just calls `ScrollToHorizontalOffset` with a fixed `ComposerActionsScrollStep` (90px) in either direction. `Grid.Row="1"` moved from `ComposerActionsScroller` itself onto the new wrapping `ComposerActionRow`, since the scroller is now nested one level deeper.
138-- Round 5 (still v170.0): the Round 4 arrows had a bug the user caught immediately — `ComposerActionsScrollLeftButton`/`ComposerActionsScrollRightButton` toggled `Visibility.Collapsed`, and since both live in `ComposerActionRow`'s outer `Auto`-width Grid columns, a `Collapsed` button drops its column to zero width. That meant the scroller's own column (the `*` one in between) grew or shrank by an arrow's width every time an arrow appeared or disappeared — the toolbar's visible footprint was resizing on every scroll-position change, not staying put while buttons moved underneath it, which is what "arrows on the left/right, toolbar size never changes" actually requires. Fixed by switching both the XAML defaults and the `ComposerActionsScroller_ScrollChanged` handler from `Visibility.Collapsed` to `Visibility.Hidden` — `Hidden` still reserves its element's layout space (it just isn't painted/hit-testable), so each arrow's `Auto` column now always sizes to the arrow's fixed width whether or not it's currently shown, and the scroller's column — and therefore the whole row's width — never changes size again. Only the buttons scrolling inside `ComposerActionsScroller` move; the row's own dimensions are now constant.
139-- Round 6 (still v170.0): a follow-up screenshot showed the fix still wasn't right — the ◀ arrow sat at the very start of the whole row, before the session actions and the Agent/Model/Effort/Permissions selectors, meaning those controls (the ones actually needed to drive the agent) scrolled out of view along with everything else whenever the mirrored config buttons didn't fit. `ComposerActionRow` was restructured from 3 columns to 4: the session-action buttons (↻✚✎🎨) and the four selectors, plus their two `Rectangle` separators, moved into their own plain `DockPanel` in column 0 — outside `ComposerActionsScroller` entirely, so they never scroll and are always fully visible. `ComposerActionsScrollLeftButton` moved from column 0 to column 1 (immediately before the scroller), `ComposerActionsScroller` moved from column 1 to column 2, and `ComposerActionsScrollRightButton` moved from column 2 to column 3 (immediately after it) — so the arrows now flank only the section that actually scrolls. `ComposerActionsScroller`'s own `DockPanel` shrank down to just the mirrored config buttons (`ComposerPromotedButtons`, `ComposerCustomCommandsButton` ⚡, `ComposerToolsButton` ☰, `ComposerSettingsButton` ⚙) — the least essential controls in the row, being duplicates of things the panel already has, so they're what gives way when space runs out. No C# changes were needed: `ComposerActionsScroller_PreviewMouseWheel`, `ComposerActionsScroller_ScrollChanged`, and the two arrow click handlers all still reference the same named elements, just with a smaller/different set of children scrolling underneath.
140-- Round 7 (still v170.0): a fresh screenshot — this time of the classic terminal-mode panel, not the native-mode composer — showed `MenuDropdownButton` (⚙ Settings/Agent Selection) missing entirely, even though every other button up to and including `ModelDropdownButton` (🤖) was visible. No code path collapses ⚙ outside `IsChatDetachedToOwnTab` (which would have hidden 🤖 too, ruling it out here), and it's declared last inside `RightButtonsPanel`. Root cause: `ControlsRow`'s `Grid.ColumnDefinitions` gave `RightButtonsPanel` an `Auto` column, which always grows to fit its content no matter how narrow the tool window is — with all 9 feature buttons promoted plus 🤖/⚙, the row's true rendered width could exceed the docked pane's actual width, and the excess silently rendered past the visible edge with no scrollbar, no arrows, and no indication anything was cut off. Fixed by applying the same essential/scrollable split already proven for the native-mode composer's action row (round 6): `RightButtonsPanel` now holds only the 9 customizable feature buttons (unchanged — `ReorderToolbarControls()` still targets it directly) inside a new `RightButtonsScroller` `ScrollViewer`, flanked by `RightButtonsScrollLeftButton`/`RightButtonsScrollRightButton` (◀/▶, `Visibility.Hidden` not `Collapsed` when not needed, same reserved-space reasoning as round 5) inside a new outer `Grid` (`RightButtonsRow`). `ToolsDropdownButton`/`CustomCommandsButton`/`ModelDropdownButton`/`MenuDropdownButton` moved into a new sibling `FixedRightButtonsPanel` that never scrolls — none of them have a fallback elsewhere if they silently disappear, unlike the 9 feature buttons, which already fall back to the ☰ Tools menu when not promoted. `ControlsRow`'s column 2 (`RightButtonsRow`) changed from `Auto` to `Star` — the actual fix, since only a bounded column gives the nested `ScrollViewer` a finite width to scroll within; the now-unused old `*` spacer column (index 1) became `Auto`. New handlers `RightButtonsScroller_PreviewMouseWheel`/`RightButtonsScrollLeftButton_Click`/`RightButtonsScrollRightButton_Click`/`RightButtonsScroller_ScrollChanged` in `ClaudeCodeControl.ProviderManagement.cs` mirror the composer's equivalents verbatim. Separately, the same screenshot's message flagged that the composer's ⚡ mirror (`ComposerCustomCommandsButton`) showed regardless of whether any custom commands were configured — unlike the panel's own `CustomCommandsButton`, which already collapses via `RefreshCustomCommandsButton()`'s `hasAny` check. Fixed by adding `_customCommandsHasItems`/`UpdateCustomCommandsButtonVisibility()` to `ChatTranscriptView` (mirroring the existing `_toolsMenuHasItems`/`UpdateToolsButtonVisibility()` pair) and a new public `SetCustomCommandsMenuHasItems(bool)`, fed from `RefreshCustomCommandsButton()` alongside its existing `CustomCommandsButton.Visibility` assignment.
141-- Round 8 (still v170.0): a follow-up screenshot in native mode showed the ⚡ Custom Commands button floating alone in the panel — every other panel toolbar control was correctly collapsed by `RefreshToolbarLayout()`'s `IsChatDetachedToOwnTab` branch, but ⚡ came back on its own. Root cause: `RefreshCustomCommandsButton()` (`ClaudeCodeControl.CustomCommands.cs`) sets `CustomCommandsButton.Visibility` unconditionally from `hasAny` alone, and it runs independently of `RefreshToolbarLayout()` — from `ApplyLoadedSettings()` at startup and after the configure-custom-commands dialog closes. Either call site, if it fired while the chat was already detached to its own tab, would silently pop ⚡ back to `Visible`, undoing the collapse with nothing else in that row visible to keep it company. Fixed by changing the assignment to `hasAny && !IsChatDetachedToOwnTab` — the composer's mirror already covers the detached case via `SetCustomCommandsMenuHasItems` (round 7). Separately, a classic terminal-mode screenshot showed an oversized, out-of-place gap between the last promoted feature button and the always-visible ⚙/🤖/☰/⚡ fixed group. Cause: `RightButtonsScroller`'s Grid.Column is `*` (Star), and when a Grid's Star column receives a genuinely bounded (not infinite) width from its parent — which is exactly what round 7's Auto→Star fix on `ControlsRow` intentionally provides — that column always consumes its *entire* proportional share for both measure and arrange, even when its actual content (the scrollable buttons) is narrower than that share; at the default `Stretch` alignment, the unused slack rendered as visible blank space between the scroller's real content and whatever sits in the next column. Fixed with one attribute — `HorizontalAlignment="Right"` on `RightButtonsScroller` — so any unused slack shifts to the scroller's own left edge (next to the ◀ arrow, itself right after the left-hand toolbar section) instead of splitting the scrollable buttons apart from the fixed group; scrolling behavior when content doesn't fit is unaffected, since in that case the scroller's desired width already equals its full allotted share and alignment has nothing left to move.
142-- Round 9 (still v170.0): two reports that the round 7/8 fixes hadn't fully landed. (1) Native mode still showed a dead vertical strip between the panel's title bar and the usage bars once the chat owned its own tab. `RefreshToolbarLayout()`'s `IsChatDetachedToOwnTab` branch collapses every *control* in that area, but two containers kept reserving height regardless: `ControlsRow` holds the ◀/▶ scroll arrows, which are deliberately `Visibility.Hidden` rather than `Collapsed` (so the toolbar's footprint doesn't jump as they come and go — see round 6), and `CheckboxRow`'s empty file-chips row still contributed its own margins. With the prompt box also auto-hidden in that state (Change B), the usage bars are the only thing the panel still owns, so the reserved height read as pure wasted space. Fixed by collapsing the two rows themselves — `Visibility panelRows = IsChatDetachedToOwnTab ? Visibility.Collapsed : Visibility.Visible;` applied to `ControlsRow` and `CheckboxRow` — which also makes the individual control collapses redundant-but-harmless and restores both rows the moment the chat docks back. (2) In classic terminal mode the ◀/▶ arrows never appeared and the row never scrolled, with ⚙ still arranged past the tool window's visible right edge. Round 7's Auto→Star fix on `ControlsRow` and round 8's `HorizontalAlignment="Right"` on the scroller were both treating symptoms of the wrong layout primitive: `RightButtonsRow` was a Grid whose columns split the available width *proportionally*, independent of what each child actually needs, so the scroller was handed a viewport wider than the panel (nothing to scroll ⇒ `ScrollableWidth == 0` ⇒ arrows stay Hidden forever) while the fixed group's column started past the visible edge. Replaced the Grid with a `DockPanel` (`LastChildFill="True"`): ◀ docks Left, then `FixedRightButtonsPanel` and ▶ dock Right (fixed group first in document order so it ends up rightmost, ▶ immediately to its left), and `RightButtonsScroller` is the last child. A DockPanel measures each docked child against the space *genuinely remaining* and gives the fill child exactly the leftover, so the fixed group can never be arranged outside the panel and the scroller's viewport is always the real available width — which is what makes `ScrollableWidth` become positive and the arrows show up. The scroller keeps round 8's `HorizontalAlignment="Right"` so slack when everything fits lands on its own left edge rather than between the promoted buttons and the fixed group. `RightButtonsScroller_ScrollChanged` also changed: it used to hide whichever arrow had nowhere left to go, so the row typically displayed a single lone arrow, which reads as decoration rather than as "there's more over here" — the reporter didn't recognize the row as scrollable at all. Now both arrows become `Visible` together as soon as `ScrollableWidth > 0.5`, with `IsEnabled` reflecting each direction so the exhausted end greys out instead of vanishing; `Hidden` (never `Collapsed`) is still the not-scrollable state, since the arrows are docked and a `Collapsed` one would give its slice back and shift the whole row.
143-- Round 10 (still v170.0): the reporter switched back to classic terminal mode and the `⚙` Settings/Agent button was simply gone from the panel's toolbar — the row ended at `🤖`, with no `⚙` past it and no `📎` in the left cluster either. Not a layout overflow (the DockPanel from round 9 was bounding the row correctly, which is why the ◀/▶ arrows were working in that same screenshot): `MenuDropdownButton.Visibility` is assigned in exactly *one* place in the whole codebase — the `if (IsChatDetachedToOwnTab)` block in `RefreshToolbarLayout()` — and that assignment only ever sets `Collapsed`. Every other control that block collapses is recomputed from scratch earlier in the same method and therefore heals on the next pass (the `Apply(...)` loop rebuilds the nine feature buttons and their menu items, `hasConsole && hasModelMenu` rebuilds `🤖`, `anyInDropdown` rebuilds `☰`), so the asymmetry went unnoticed; `⚙`, `📎` `AttachDropdownButton`, `▶` `SendPromptButton` and `⚡` `CustomCommandsButton` have no such authority. Once the chat had been detached to its own tab even briefly, those four were collapsed for good — turning native mode off dropped straight past the branch with nothing restoring them, and `⚙` in particular has no fallback anywhere (it is not part of the customizable toolbar, so it can't be re-promoted, and the Settings dialog is only reachable through it). 173	## Generate Commit Message (CommitMessage.cs, v134.0; Commit and Push sibling v205.0)
174	
175	- Purpose: toolbar/☰ Tools button that asks the active agent to draft a commit message from the current git diff and fills it into Visual Studio's built-in Git Changes tool window, ready for the user to review alongside the diff before committing. Never commits automatically.
176	- Sibling feature (v205.0), `GenerateCommitMessageCommitAndPushAsync` / `ToolbarButton.GenerateCommitMessageAndPush` (🚀): runs the identical drafting flow (see below — both share `GenerateCommitMessageCoreAsync`), then (v247.0) skips the Git Changes fill entirely and runs straight through to the repository with no confirmation prompt (Daniel: remove the confirm step — the toolbar/☰ click or "On Agent Finish" preset pick already is the confirmation). `git add -A` (stage everything, matching what VS's own "Commit All" would stage — including new untracked files the diff-based draft never saw, since `git diff HEAD` does not report untracked files), then `git commit -F <tempfile>` (the message is written to a private temp file under `%TEMP%\ClaudeCodeVS_Session\<guid>\commit-message.txt` and passed via `-F` rather than `-m "<text>"`, sidestepping command-line quoting/newline fragility for a multi-line message), then `git push`. Each step uses `RunGitDetailed` (GitSync.cs — exit code + stderr, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`/`GCM_INTERACTIVE=never` so a credential prompt fails fast instead of hanging) and stops with an error `MessageBox` (including stderr) on the first failing step; a failed push after a successful commit is called out explicitly since the commit already exists locally. Success is silent (v210.0 removed the success `MessageBox`); only failures show a `MessageBox`. No Git Changes interaction (v247.0): earlier versions filled the box before committing and cleared it after, but `TryFillGitChangesCommitMessageAsync` activates the Git Changes window and calls `SetForegroundWindow` on the VS main window, stealing focus from whatever app the user was in when the run (often an "On Agent Finish" follow-up) completed. The fill was immediately cleared after the commit anyway, so both calls were dropped.
177	- No AI co-author (v205.0): the drafting prompt (`BuildCommitMessagePrompt`) explicitly tells the model not to add a "Co-Authored-By" line or any AI attribution/signature, and `CleanCommitMessage` defensively strips any line starting with `Co-Authored-By:` (case-insensitive) via `StripAiAttributionLines` regardless — some agents append that line out of their own default habit even when asked not to. Applies to both Generate Commit Message and its Commit and Push sibling, since both share the same drafting/cleanup path. v220.0: `IsAiAttributionLine` also drops "Generated with/by <agent>" footers and lines with an AI vendor noreply address, ignoring markdown/invisible prefixes; and since the raw reply is still rendered in the chat, `ReplaceCommitReplyInTranscriptAsync` swaps that reply row's text for the cleaned message (`ChatMessageViewModel.ReplaceText`) once the transcript drain has completed the row (polls up to ~3 s, only if the row cleans to the same message).
178	- "On Agent Finish" follow-up preset (v205.0): the follow-up field's "Preset ▾" menu (AgentFinishDialog.cs) gained a "Generate Commit Message, Commit and Push" entry alongside the existing "Generate Commit Message" one, backed by a second flag, `AgentFinishConfig.FollowUpGenerateCommitMessageAndPush`, mutually exclusive with `FollowUpGenerateCommitMessage`. `RunFollowUpAsync` checks the Commit-and-Push flag first. Picking either flag-driven preset now clears the follow-up textbox instead of writing a placeholder label into it (`SetFollowUpText(string.Empty, ...)`) — the box's saved text is never actually read when a flag is set, so filling it with e.g. "Generate Commit Message" was a dead cosmetic string; the notification label is derived from the flags directly (`OnAgentTurnCompletedAsync`'s `followLabel`), not from the box.
179	- Gating: requires Native Mode (`IsNativeModeActive`) — the terminal path has no reliable way to capture a clean text answer (only screen-scraping, already used elsewhere as a frail last resort unfit for feeding a text box). Clicking with terminal mode active or no agent running shows an explanatory `MessageBox` instead of doing nothing.
180	- Diff collection: reuses `FindGitRepositoryRoot`/`RunGitCommand` from `Diff.cs` (`git diff HEAD`, `GitDiffTimeoutMs = 15000`). No changes → `MessageBox` and abort.
181	- Prompt: instructs the model to reply with only the commit message (conventional-commit style summary ≤72 chars, optional short body, no code fences). Diffs over `LargeCommitDiffThresholdChars` (1024, same threshold as `BuildErrors.cs`) are written to a temp file under `%TEMP%\ClaudeCodeVS_Session\<guid>\` and referenced by path instead of pasted inline, converted to a WSL path via `ConvertToWslPath` for WSL providers — avoids paste fragility and keeps the raw diff out of the chat transcript.
182	- Response capture (`CaptureNextAssistantTurnAsync`): resolves the same session `SendTextToAgentAsync` would use (`ResolveFocusedNativeSessionId()` → focused tab's `NativeChatSessionState.AgentSession` or the default `_agentSession`), then subscribes a *second*, temporary handler to that session's `IAgentSession.Received` — a plain multicast `EventHandler<AgentEvent>`, so this tap runs alongside the existing UI-rendering subscriber (`OnAgentEventReceived`) without disturbing normal chat rendering. Accumulates `AssistantText` chunks and resolves on `TurnCompleted` (or `null` on `SessionError` / after `SideQuestionTimeoutMs`). Works identically for every provider since it only depends on the normalized `AgentEvent` stream, not a provider-specific `--print` subprocess. The capture is armed *before* `SendTextToAgentAsync` is awaited, so no chunk can be missed.
183	- Git Changes automation (`TryFillGitChangesCommitMessageAsync`): there is no supported VS API to read/write the modern Git Changes commit box (`IChangesExt.CommitMessage` is Team Explorer-era and no longer wired to it), so this is deliberately best-effort UI Automation, matching the pattern already used in `AgentCompletion.cs`'s console-detection code (`System.Windows.Automation.AutomationElement`, fully qualified — this file also does not `using System.Windows.Automation;`). Opens/focuses the window via `dte.Windows` caption match or, failing that, tries each command name in `GitChangesCommandCandidates` (`"Team.Git.Changes"`, `"View.GitChanges"` — unconfirmed across VS versions, sequential fallback). Then does a bounded BFS (`FindDescendantByNameContains`, capped at 6000 nodes) for the "Git Changes" subtree, and within it picks the tallest `ControlType.Edit` element supporting `ValuePattern` (`FindCommitMessageEditElement`) as a heuristic for the multiline commit box vs. the window's single-line file filter box — WPF exposes no reliable "is multiline" automation property here.
184	- Any failure in the automation path (window/command not found, element not found, `ElementNotAvailableException`, etc.) is swallowed and reported as `false`; the caller then copies the message to the clipboard via the existing `ClipboardRetryAsync` helper and shows a "paste with Ctrl+V" notice — the feature can never silently fail to deliver the generated message.
185	- Fragility note: since the Git Changes automation tree isn't a stable public contract, a future VS update could break the heuristic silently (no exception, just "not found" → clipboard fallback engages). If this starts happening often, re-verify the tree shape with the Windows `Inspect.exe` tool against the VS version in use.

187	## Recommend AI Model (ModelRecommendation.cs, Agents/ModelRecommender.cs, v213.0)
188	
189	- Purpose: toolbar/☰ Tools action (`ToolbarButton.RecommendModel`, 💡). The user types a prompt, clicks it, and Opus at Extra High effort says which Claude model and effort fit that prompt; a dialog shows the answer with model/effort pickers preselected to it, and *Apply* switches. The prompt is never sent. Claude Code / Claude Code (WSL) only — offered for every agent like the other toolbar features (#97) and explained by a `MessageBox` at click time otherwise.
190	- A separate one-shot CLI, not the live session: asking the running agent would add a turn to the user's conversation, and in terminal mode there is no clean way to read an answer back (the reason Generate Commit Message needs native mode). So it works the same in terminal and native mode, with or without an agent running. Built on the `/btw` side-question plumbing (`AskSideQuestionAsync`): `JsonLineProcessHost`, prompt over stdin, EOF ends it.
191	- Command line (`ClaudeCommandBuilder.GetModelRecommendationArguments`): `--print --model opus --effort xhigh --output-format json --json-schema <schema> --system-prompt <rubric> --tools "" --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence --disable-slash-commands`. `--system-prompt` replaces the full agent prompt; `--tools ""` stops it exploring the repo; `--no-session-persistence` keeps every click out of Session History (measured: no project folder entry is written).
192	- Measured (CLI 2.1.285, Opus 5.5): 6–9 s per answer, xhigh adds only ~2 s on harder prompts. The CLI prints one `type: result` line whose `structured_output` holds the schema-validated object (`result` repeats it as text).
193	- Runs in the workspace on purpose: the project's CLAUDE.md is still loaded (it is user context, not the system prompt), which raised the input from ~1.3k to ~11k tokens in this repo but made the advice project-aware (it priced in this repo's version-bump/README rules). The 1h prompt cache makes repeat clicks cheap; the first click in a while costs the most (~$0.09 measured here).
194	- Command-line safety of the rubric: `ModelRecommender.SystemPrompt` is one line with no `& | < > ^ % !`, double quotes, backslashes, `$` or backticks — an npm `claude.cmd` shim re-parses arguments through cmd.exe (a newline ends the command, `%` expands inside quotes) and the WSL path nests it inside `bash -lic`. Guarded by `SystemPrompt_SurvivesCmdShimsAndBash`. The schema's quotes go through the existing `QuoteArgument` path; the exact WSL string was verified end to end through `ProcessStartInfo` → `wsl.exe` → `bash -lic`.
195	- Rubric/schema: models `haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus`/`fable`, efforts `low`..`max` (enums in the schema, so the CLI rejects anything else). Ultracode is left out — a workflow mode, not an amount of thinking — but the dialog's effort picker still offers it; Opus Plan is not offered (no headless equivalent) and maps to Opus when it is the current pick. The prompt is fenced in `<task>` tags in `BuildRequest` so instructions inside it read as the task being sized; over 30k chars it is truncated.
196	- Parser (`ModelRecommender.ParseOutput`, pure, `Tests/ModelRecommenderTests.cs`): scans lines from the end for the result envelope (a WSL login shell's profile can print first), `is_error: true` surfaces the CLI's own text ("Not logged in…"), falls back to the outermost `{…}` in `result` for a CLI that ignores `--json-schema`, normalizes "Extra High"/"x-high" to `xhigh`. Empty stdout reports stderr instead (CLI missing in the distro, bad custom path).
197	- Where the prompt comes from — and so where the result is applied (`GetPromptForRecommendation`): in native mode the focused parallel tab's composer first (`ResolveFocusedNativeSessionId`), then the default chat's composer when it is the live input (`HasComposerInput`), and the panel's `PromptTextBox` in every mode as the fallback. Only the first case targets a parallel tab.
198	- Dialog: opens immediately with an indeterminate progress bar and the pickers on the *current* pair; the advisor starts on `Loaded` and moves the pickers to the recommendation when it arrives. Closing the dialog cancels the token, which kills the process tree through `JsonLineProcessHost.Dispose`. On failure the status line shows the error and the pickers stay usable for a manual pick.
199	- Applying (`ApplyRecommendedModelAsync`), only the parts that changed: a parallel tab switches its own `NativeChatSessionState` (unpersisted, like its composer pickers); otherwise `_settings` is updated and saved (Max/Ultracode stay session-only through `IsSessionOnlyEffort`/`_lastPersistableEffortLevel`), then a native chat switches live — model, then effort — and relaunches with resume once if either live switch is refused (never two relaunches); the terminal gets `/model <alias>`, an 800 ms gap, then `/effort <level>`, the same commands the 🤖 menu types. Model goes first so the effort is applied to the model it was chosen for.

Yes, it's fixed and shipped as v312.0. The comment in the screenshot matched real bugs. Tests passed, it's published to the Marketplace, and it's committed and pushed as `acd486e`. I haven't tried it in a running VS (no F5 run), but I checked every value the fix relies on against your open VS 2026.

**What was wrong**
- **Opening the window never worked.** The extension tried two commands, `Team.Git.Changes` and `View.GitChanges`, and neither exists. The real one is `View.GitWindow`. So if Git Changes was closed, the message always went to the clipboard, even in English VS.
- **Finding the window only worked in English.** It searched for the caption "Git Changes", which is translated in other VS languages, such as the Chinese one the commenter seems to use.
- **When that search failed, it could fill the wrong box.** It fell back to the tallest text box anywhere in VS, which is the extension's own chat input (352 px tall here, versus 138 px for the commit box). It would put the message there and report success.

**The fix** (`Controls/ClaudeCodeControl.CommitMessage.cs`)
- The window is found by its internal ID, which is the same in every language, and is always brought to the front. A background tab exposes none of its contents to the search.
- The commit box is found by its internal name (`commentTextBox`). The fallback only looks inside the Git Changes window, never across all of VS.
- Hidden, disabled or read-only boxes are skipped. After writing, it reads the box back, and if the message didn't stick it copies it to the clipboard instead.

**Release and commit**
- **Release:** the version is now 312.0 in all three places, with a README entry and an updated section in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **Publish:** `publish.cmd` hit the usual VsixPub0031 sign-in error, and its built-in retry got the upload through.
- **Commit:** the author is only `dliedke`, with no Co-Authored-By line and no mention of AI in the message. However, the Entire hook added an `Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7N…` line to the end of the commit message and pushed 2 checkpoint refs alongside it. That line links to this session but doesn't name a model. Removing it would mean rewriting the pushed commit and force-pushing `master`, so I haven't done that. Tell me if you want it removed.
